text:
maria: Heads-up — the headroom dashboard is showing sustained low headroom in gpool-us-west-2. queue_depth >= 0.8 for ~18m, GPUs reporting near-saturation. autoscaler didn't kick.
kevin: saw it. prometheus shows batch_size jumped from 8 -> 20 for some routes, latency spiked. looks like continuous batching pushed pods to 100% util.
sam: can confirm. k8s nodegroup for that AZ is at max-size (no remaining capacity to scale). cluster-autoscaler logs show 'no more ASGs to grow'.
maria: hmm. is this a config/state drift or real traffic? any deployment or rollout around 17:32?
deploy-bot: @channel deploy/redwood-serving v2.14 -> v2.15 promoted to gpool-us-west-2 at 1752145200. Canary passed.
tara: the rollout coincides with the batch size change — maybe new runtime has a batching change. we should have a recording rule for "serving_headroom" instead of inferring from queue_depth alone.
kevin:Agreed — proposed PromQL (quick):

  # headroom as fraction of available batch slots across GPUs
  sum(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"}) - sum(serving_in_flight_batches)
  / sum(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"})

  But we should use a rate or per-minute window and guard against division by zero.
maria: Also suggest we switch alerting from absolute queue_depth to a smoothed headroom metric and require 5m for firing to avoid flapping. current alert: queue_depth > 0.7 for 1m — too noisy.
tara: +1. Proposed alert rule text:

  ALERT LowServingHeadroom
  IF (recording:serving_headroom:ratio:5m) < 0.12
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity = "page" }
  ANNOTATIONS { runbook = "link_to_headroom_runbook" }

sam: runbook should include quick remediation steps:
- check nodegroup quotas in cloud console
- bump max-size temporarily or launch emergency spot pool
- rollback runtime change if batching param is culprit
- route heavy customers to dedicated pools (if configured)
- add synthetic load test after changes

kevin: ops note — increasing max-size will increase cost. we should add a dashboard panel showing cost delta for +N nodes by region so product/finance can make tradeoffs.
maria: For immediate mitigation I scaled the deployment replicas down for the offending route (cheap stopgap) and set a per-route max_batch_size env override to 10. latency dropped, queue_depth starting to fall.
ops-bot: Incident ticket CREATED: #INC-2025-114 (autosc-queue-headroom) assigned to eng-infra oncall.
tara: follow-ups: 1) add recording rule and new alert in staging 2) add per-region headroom panel (percentiles, not raw averages) 3) make a probe for autoscaler coverage (simulate burst of small requests) 4) playbook update for nodegroup max-size checks
sam: I'll own the recording rule + alert PR. kevin, can you sketch the cost-impact panel mock? maria — can you paste the before/after charts from your temporary mitigation in the ticket?
kevin: will do. also let's include a histogram of batch_size per-route — that helped us spot the new runtime behavior.
maria: pasted charts in the incident ticket. thanks all. :thumbsup:
kevin: re: long-term — we should consider soft-headroom (reserve 10% capacity) vs on-demand cold-starts. tradeoff doc next week?
tara: yes, add to roadmap. for now, PRs: #234 (recording rule), #235 (alert), #236 (dashboards).
